title: Signed two-factor shifts commute with the lax localization tensorator
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $C$ be its category of $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $Q:\operatorname{Ch}(C)\to D(\mathcal O_X)$ be the localization with the specified K-flat derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Write $\mu_{K,L}:QK\otimes^{\mathbf L}QL\to Q\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes L)$ for its canonical lax monoidal comparison [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor]. For arbitrary integer complexes $K,L$ and integers $a,b$, let $s_{a,b}:\operatorname{Tot}(K[a]\otimes L[b])\to\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes L)[a+b]$ multiply the summand with shifted first-factor degree $i$ by $(-1)^{bi}$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]. Let $t_{a,b}:QK[a]\otimes^{\mathbf L}QL[b]\to(QK\otimes^{\mathbf L}QL)[a+b]$ be its K-flat descended comparison [lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent], and let $\eta_{K,a}:Q(K[a])\xrightarrow{\sim}(QK)[a]$ be the localization shift comparison. Then
$$\eta_{\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes L),a+b}\,Q(s_{a,b})\,\mu_{K[a],L[b]}=\mu_{K,L}[a+b]\,t_{a,b}\,(\eta_{K,a}\otimes^{\mathbf L}\eta_{L,b}).$$
This is an equality of derived morphisms from $Q(K[a])\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q(L[b])$ to $Q\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes L)[a+b]$. No flatness, boundedness, acyclicity or quasi-coherence is assumed on $K,L$, and $\mu$ is not asserted invertible.

proof.text: Put $n=a+b$ and $T(K,L)=\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes L)$. Extract the second shift first, then the first: $s_{a,b}=s^1_a[b]\circ s^2_b$ on $(K[a],L[b])$. Its sign on shifted first degree $i$ is $(-1)^{bi}$. This is natural in chain maps in both variables by the total-shift theorem. For clarity, the first-differential signs in $s\,d$ and $d\,s$ are respectively $a+b(i+1)$ and $bi+a+b$; the second-differential signs are $i+b+bi$ and $bi+a+b+(i+a)$, equal modulo two. Thus this convention works for all integers, including negative ones.

proof.text: On the small site of open subsets of $X$, choose flat-term K-flat resolutions $p:P\to K$ and $q:R\to L$. Shifts preserve flat-term K-flat complexes. Since localization inverts quasi-isomorphisms and commutes with shifts, $Q(p[a])$ and $Q(q[b])$ are isomorphisms. Hence $v=Q(p[a])\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q(q[b])$ is invertible, with inverse the tensor of their inverses.

proof.text: The site derived tensor descent says that a natural transformation between bifunctors on $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is determined by, and extends uniquely from, its restriction to pairs of flat-term K-flat complexes. Hence the native tensor of the statement and the published bifunctor $T$ of shift descent are identified by the unique natural isomorphism whose component at such a pair $(P,R)$ is $c_{P,R}\circ\mu_{P,R}$, where $c$ is the published representative comparison $QT(P,R)\cong T(QP,QR)$; $t_{a,b}$ is read through this identification, as the statement does. Under it, the simultaneous K-flat comparison of the native tensor theorem is $c=\mu_{P,R}^{-1}$, also on shifted pairs. The normalization clause of derived-tensor shift descent, composed in the extraction order of step 1, says $\eta\,Q(s_{a,b})\,\mu_{P[a],R[b]}=\mu_{P,R}[n]\,t_{a,b}\,(\eta_{P,a}\otimes^{\mathbf L}\eta_{R,b})$: $t^2_b$ at $(Q(P[a]),QR)$ and $t^1_a$ at $(QP,QR)$ are $Q(s^2_b)$, $Q(s^1_a)$ conjugated by $c$ and $\eta$, and naturality of $t^2_b$ in the first variable along $\eta_{P,a}$ moves its first argument from $Q(P[a])$ to $(QP)[a]$. This is precisely the desired equality on the resolving pair: it follows by substituting $c=\mu^{-1}$ in the stated conjugation formula and cancelling the adjacent inverse comparisons.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor; signed normalization from more-algebra.tex Tag 0FNH, item-shift-tensor. Agent assembly of the cited representative comparisons.

proof.text: Call the two sides at $(K,L)$ $A_{K,L}$ and $B_{K,L}$, and put $w=Q(T(p,q))[n]$. Naturality of $\mu$, $s$, and $\eta$ gives $A_{K,L}v=wA_{P,R}$. Naturality of the descended $t$ and of $\eta$, followed by naturality of $\mu$ shifted by $n$, gives $B_{K,L}v=wB_{P,R}$. Step 3 therefore gives $A_{K,L}v=B_{K,L}v$; compose on the right with $v^{-1}$. This proves the displayed equality without inverting $w$ or $\mu_{K,L}$.
